_doc: D30 / referee_r8/AUMIC_SCALE_TEST.md, 2026-09-27.  The FIRST ON-SKY VALIDATION of the parallax amplitude-loss model of Sec. sec:parallax, and a geometry-free check of the absolute flux scale.  Project 2024.1.01095.S writes the star's APPARENT position into FIELD::PHASE_DIR (the pipeline's barycentric offset and the independently computed annual-parallax displacement cancel to 0.1-0.2 mas at all ten retained executions, through a 3.8x change in magnitude and a ~170 degree rotation), so a phase-centre estimator sits on the star and its amplitudes carry NO positional error.  Our legacy star_lm() extractor was run on the SAME visibilities at the SAME timestamps, so the ratio (ours)/(theirs) isolates our own positional loss.  The two epochs are in different configurations, which is the whole point: January is geometry-free and measures our absolute scale, May is at 0.42 beams and measures the loss model.  Comparison amplitudes are from White et al. (2026), an independent reduction of the same visibilities; every other number is measured here.
